guard_streams.source: 24 million UK homes can get gigabit broadband
guard_streams.write_limit: National coverage percentages from a dated Connected Nations snapshot are not proof of current availability or orderability for a selected parcel.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the coverage update on 24 April 2024.
The update reported 24 million UK homes able to get gigabit-capable broadband.
This represented 80% of UK homes.
Gigabit-capable availability was up from 73% one year earlier.
The underlying Connected Nations snapshot was as of January 2024.
Full-fibre broadband was available to 62% of households.
Full-fibre availability was up from 48% year on year.
Premises unable to get decent broadband fell to 57,000.
The previous-year count of premises without decent broadband was 68,000.
Outdoor 5G from at least one operator was available at 92% of premises, up from 82%.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom reveals most complained-about telecoms and pay-TV providers
guard_streams.write_limit: Historic complaint rates and provider rankings are service-quality comparisons, not selected-parcel broadband coverage or speed evidence.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the complaints update on 18 October 2022.
The page was last updated on 16 March 2023.
The figures cover the three months from April to June.
Overall complaint volumes were broadly in line with the previous three months.
Shell Energy generated the most broadband and landline complaints.
Shell Energy had 31 broadband complaints per 100,000 customers.
Sky had three broadband complaints per 100,000 customers.
The broadband industry average was 11 complaints per 100,000 customers.
Shell Energy had 23 home-phone complaints per 100,000 customers.
Virgin Media had ten pay-TV complaints per 100,000 customers.

guard_streams.source: Bulletin: BDUK delivery performance, quarterly: October 2025 to Dec 2025
guard_streams.write_limit: Official delivery statistics are aggregated, revised programme outputs and cannot establish current live service or measured speed for a selected parcel.

facts.detail: BDUK published the quarterly bulletin on 19 February 2026.
The release covers 1 October to 31 December 2025.
BDUK estimated 56,000 premises received gigabit-capable coverage in the quarter.
Cumulative delivery by BDUK gigabit programmes reached an estimated 1,373,800 premises.
GIS contracts delivered 41,830 premises, or 75% of quarterly delivery.
Vouchers delivered 10,150 premises, or 18%.
Superfast and Hubs delivered 4,050 premises, or 7%.
Residential premises represented 50,200, or 90%, of quarterly delivery.
England accounted for 45,100 premises, or 80%, of quarterly delivery.
Yorkshire and the Humber had the highest English regional delivery at 8,700 premises.

guard_streams.source: Bulletin: BDUK Delivery Performance, annual: April 2025 to March 2026
guard_streams.write_limit: Annual official statistics are revised aggregate delivery records and cannot prove current orderability or measured performance for a selected parcel.

facts.detail: BDUK published the annual bulletin on 11 June 2026.
The release covers the 2025/26 financial year.
BDUK interventions delivered gigabit-capable coverage to 192,570 premises.
Annual delivery increased by 42,280 premises, or 28%, from the previous year.
Cumulative BDUK gigabit delivery reached 1,418,410 premises.
GIS contracts accounted for 139,490 premises, or 72%, of annual delivery.
Voucher schemes contributed 30,530 premises, or 16%.
Rural areas represented 173,190 premises, or 90%, of annual delivery.
England accounted for 145,110 premises, or 75%, of annual delivery.
An estimated 43,880 delivered premises previously lacked superfast availability of at least 30 Mbit/s.

guard_streams.source: Bulletin: BDUK delivery performance, quarterly: April 2025 to Sept 2025
guard_streams.write_limit: Quarterly programme statistics are aggregate, revision-prone delivery records and cannot verify current serviceability or speed at a selected parcel.

facts.detail: BDUK published the two-quarter bulletin on 13 November 2025.
The release covers 1 April to 30 September 2025.
BDUK estimated delivery of 44,000 premises in Q1 2025/26.
BDUK estimated delivery of 36,200 premises in Q2 2025/26.
Cumulative delivery by BDUK gigabit programmes reached 1,307,200 premises.
GIS contracts delivered 57,210 premises, or 71%, across the two quarters.
Vouchers delivered 14,460 premises, or 18%.
Superfast and Hubs delivered 8,590 premises, or 11%.
Residential premises represented 71,500, or 89%, of delivery.
BDUK recorded ongoing work on UPRN identification and voucher-data quality.
